newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close at record after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close at record after U.S. data.

text.p: 1450 GMT - Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher to hitting a record closing high after thje U.S. employment cost index report led to a sharp rise in late trade.

Dealers noted the U.S. employment data, which is considered an important indicator of U.S. inflation trends, was favourable for the markets. Gains in government bond futures and positive corporate news also helped shares. One trader also pointed out that the U.S. dollar is still on a high level against the Swiss franc, although the U.S. currency lost some ground today.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 61.8 points, or 1.29 percent, for a a record close of 4,855.1.
A new all-time high was reached at 4,864.3 points.
* Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 33.39 points, or 1.1 percent, to 3,070.95.
Total bourse turover stood as 2.23 billion francs.
Dealers said shares were also lifted by U.S. durable goods data and U.S. consumer confidence data, both of which were weaker than expected.

* UBS bearer shares topped the active list, rocketing 33 francs, or 2.44 percent, to 1,386. Dealers explained the rise with several buy recommendation due to technical factors and fundamental reasons.
The other two major banks, SBC and CS Group were also more than one percent firmer.
* Among insurers, Zurich soared 10.5 francs to 475 ahead of 1996 results which are expected on Wednesday after bourse close. Swiss Re and Winterthur also gained ground.

* Novartis registered shares rose 21 francs to 1,914. Roche certificates climbed 180 francs to 12,355. Clariant, whose first-quarter sales rise of 11 percent in local currencies was better than expected, firmed 13 francs to 843.
* Alusuisse was down on profit taking, losing 21 francs to 1,250. ABB rose five francs to 1,769.
* Options on UBS were in the limelight on the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex).

One dealer said UBS options were actively sought, refelcting demand for UBS shares on the cash market. Turnover of UBS options was 45,806 calls and 36,737 puts, accounting for around half of the total turnover of 165,321 options. The total call/put ratio was at 1.26 to one.
In SMI futures, 5,437 SMI contracts changed hands. The May SMI was up 61.1 points to 4,856.0. The futures was temporarily traded at a premium of 10 points due to today's U.S. data.
